slides.texte_overlay:
How to wake up
without feeling tired
Wake up at the same time every day, weekends too. Your body loves rhythm. After two weeks, you'll start waking up naturally just before your alarm.
Get light in your eyes within ten minutes. Open the curtains or step outside. Morning light tells your brain the day has started and clears the fog fast.
Drink a big glass of water first. After eight hours without drinking, your body is a little dehydrated. Water before coffee wakes you up surprisingly well.
Stop hitting snooze. Every snooze starts a new sleep cycle you never finish, which makes you groggier. Put your alarm across the room if you need to.
Give your mind something good to start with. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it wakes my brain up better than scrolling.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It wakes my brain up better than scrolling.

slides.texte_overlay: Move for five minutes. Stretches, push-ups, a quick walk. Getting blood flowing tells your body it's time to be awake. Small changes, big mornings.
Fix your evenings. Screens off an hour before bed, a cool dark room, no late heavy meals. Great mornings always start the night before.
